question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>KBr</mi></math> is doped with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></math> mole percent of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>SrBr</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> The number of cationic vacancies in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>KBr</mi></math> crystal is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>14</mn></msup></math>. (Round off to the Nearest Integer). [Atomic Mass :  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>39</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>Br</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>79</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></math>,<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open=""><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>023</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>23</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>

solution.text:
1 mole KBr (=119gm) have 10-5100 moles SrBr2 and hence, 10-7 moles cation vacancy (as 1Sr2+ will result 1 cation vacancy)

∴ Required number of cation vacancies

=10-7×6.023×1023119=5.06×1014≃5×1014
